diagnoses.label: amount_tier_candidate_selection_misordered_in_split_summary_block
diagnoses.general_pattern: When multiple lines in the SAME priority tier contain a monetary token and the OCR produces slightly different values across them (e.g., 'Total incl. of GST 102.00' earlier plus 'Total Amt Rounded 702.00' later within the same pre-cutoff summary block), the extractor accepts the LAST matching candidate without using corroboration from adjacent non-tier anchors (Subtotal, Payment, Cash − Change). The late candidate is often the OCR-corrupted outlier (e.g., '702.00' vs. the true '102.00' corroborated by Subtotal/Payment).
diagnoses.wrong_approach: Iterating same-tier candidates strictly from last to first and accepting the first parseable monetary token, with no cross-check against subtotal/payment/change on the same receipt. This systematically picks garbled trailing lines (e.g., 'Total Amt Rounded ——S«702.00') over cleanly-anchored earlier totals in the same tier.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: 074.jpg: predicted total_amount='702.00'; receipt image shows Subtotal 102.00, Total Excl./Incl. of GST 102.00, Total Amt Rounded 102.00, Payment 102.00; the trailing '702.00' only appears in an OCR-garbled 'Total Amt Rounded ——S«702.00' line in one variant. Trajectory think-note e0025 explicitly reasons that '102.00 appears at: Subtotal 102.00, Total incl. 102.00, Payment 102.00' and '702.00 appears at: Total Amt Rounded 702.00' but the chosen rule still returns 702.00. Verifier field_feedback: 074.jpg amount_correct=false while date_correct=true.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: Before accepting a same-tier candidate, cross-check its value against other total-adjacent anchors on the receipt (Subtotal, Total Incl./Excl. of GST on neighbouring lines, Payment, Cash − Change). Prefer the candidate whose value is corroborated by ≥1 non-tier anchor over an uncorroborated outlier, even when the outlier appears later in the text or has the same tier rank.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Within a single tier, score each candidate by (a) cleanliness of the line (no stray non-[0-9.,] glyphs inside the numeric span) and (b) corroborated_support from Subtotal / Total Incl./Excl. of GST / Payment / (Cash − Change) within rounding tolerance. Accept the candidate with the highest corroborated_support; break ties by position (last) only when no anchor evidence distinguishes them. Keep tier priority strictly dominant over this intra-tier scoring.
diagnoses.scope_boundary: Applies only to receipt-style OCR tasks that declare a tier/exclusion keyword list AND where multiple same-tier total lines appear in the same summary block. Does not apply to tasks with a single total line, to non-receipt documents, or to tier-priority ordering itself.
diagnoses.do_not_generalize_to: Do not weaken the strict tier-priority ordering, do not import this corroboration logic into non-receipt OCR or openai-vision, and do not use consensus to override a cleanly-anchored higher-priority tier.
diagnoses.target_section: Structured Field Extraction from Receipts > Mechanism anchor: multi_variant_consensus_over_tier_priority

diagnoses.label: truncated_two_decimal_token_accepted_in_higher_tier_blocks_better_variant
diagnoses.general_pattern: When OCR truncates a monetary token's last digit (e.g., '88.17' → '88.1'), the extractor still accepts the one-decimal number from a higher-priority tier (e.g., 'TOTAL RM 88.1') and formats it to '88.10' via f'{v:.2f}'. This silently pads a truncated value to two decimals and locks in the wrong amount instead of falling back to another OCR variant that produced the full two-decimal number ('88.17') on the same tier line.
diagnoses.wrong_approach: Treating any token with a decimal point (including one-decimal '88.1') as a valid monetary candidate and formatting with '{:.2f}', so a tier-1/tier-2 match on a truncated token outranks a later variant's clean two-decimal match on the same tier.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: 064.jpg: predicted total_amount='88.10'; receipt image clearly shows 'Total RM 88.17' and 'Total Gross C RM 88.17'. Trajectory think-note e0028 observes: 'Default: tier=1 (TOTAL RM), value=88.10 (from 88.1)' vs 'Preprocessed: Total Gross C RM 88.17 → 88.17 correct', and concludes the default OCR truncated 88.17 to 88.1 but was still accepted. Verifier field_feedback: 064.jpg amount_correct=false; a later exchange (e0029) attempted to tighten NUM_RE to exactly two decimal digits but the final written workbook still contains '88.10' at row for 064.jpg, i.e., the two-decimal invariant did not propagate to the delivered output.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: Enforce the two-decimal structural invariant at candidate-selection time, not only at formatting time: reject tokens that match only one fractional digit (e.g., \d+\.\d{1}) as OCR-truncated, and prefer any other same-tier candidate (including from a different OCR variant) that yields exactly two fractional digits.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Define the monetary regex for totals as requiring exactly two fractional digits ((?<![\w.])(?:\d{1,3}(?:,\d{3})+|\d+)\.\d{2}(?![\w.\d])). Treat one-decimal matches as truncation artefacts and discard them in favour of (a) another same-tier candidate in the same variant with two decimals, or (b) a cross-variant same-tier candidate with two decimals. Never pad '.X' to '.X0' silently.
diagnoses.scope_boundary: Scoped to receipt total extraction where the task contract specifies two-decimal monetary strings. Does not apply to prices/quantities, non-monetary numbers, or tasks whose contract explicitly accepts one-decimal values.
diagnoses.do_not_generalize_to: Do not apply the strict two-decimal regex to generic number parsing, to unit prices, to GST/tax rates, or to non-receipt skills.
diagnoses.target_section: Structured Field Extraction from Receipts > Mechanism anchor: monetary_two_decimal_invariant

diagnoses.label: ambiguous_dmy_vs_mdy_binding_on_isolated_receipt
diagnoses.general_pattern: On a receipt whose date tokens have both components ≤12 (e.g., '09/08/2018'), the extractor commits to one locale ordering without using a batch-level dominance signal or an explicit locale declaration. When the overall batch is Malaysian DD/MM/YYYY, a solitary ambiguous row can still be parsed as MM/DD/YYYY and silently ISO-formatted, producing a wrong date even though the raw OCR of the receipt was correct.
diagnoses.wrong_approach: Parsing each date-shaped token in isolation with a fixed ordering (or defaulting to MDY) instead of (a) using the task-declared locale when present, (b) inferring the dominant ordering from unambiguous rows in the same batch (any component >12 fixes the ordering), and (c) only then resolving still-ambiguous rows under that dominant ordering.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: 034.jpg: predicted date='2018-08-09'; receipt image shows 'Date: 09/03/2018' with other batch rows (e.g., 018.jpg '18/03/2018', 030.jpg '30/03/2018') having first components >12 that unambiguously fix DD/MM/YYYY ordering. Verifier field_feedback: 034.jpg date_correct=false, amount_correct=true. Note: evidence shows a locale-ordering mismatch; the specific true calendar date is not inferred here.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: Run a two-pass date resolution: pass 1 collects (component1, component2, year) triples across all receipts and marks each row as 'unambiguous DMY', 'unambiguous MDY', or 'ambiguous'; pass 2 chooses locale by (declared locale) → (dominant unambiguous ordering) → (fall back to DMY for Malaysian receipt corpora if that is the declared convention) and resolves ambiguous rows accordingly.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: In receipt_date_label_binding_and_locale, make batch-dominance inference explicit and executable: before writing any row, scan all extracted date triples for the batch, derive the dominant ordering from unambiguous rows, and only then format each row's ISO date. Keep per-row label-binding (DATE vs PRINT/CLOSED/LOYALTY) separate from locale resolution.
diagnoses.scope_boundary: Scoped to receipt batches with mixed ambiguous/unambiguous rows and no explicit per-receipt locale label. Does not override an unambiguous row based on batch majority; does not apply to non-receipt date fields or to tasks that declare locale per row.
diagnoses.do_not_generalize_to: Do not import batch-dominance logic into single-document tasks, into xlsx date formatting for financial models, or into generic date parsers in pdf/openai-vision skills.
diagnoses.target_section: Structured Field Extraction from Receipts > Mechanism anchor: receipt_date_label_binding_and_locale

diagnoses.label: failed_extraction_written_as_empty_string_instead_of_null
diagnoses.general_pattern: When total extraction fails for a receipt, the writeback path emits an empty string ('') rather than Python None, so the resulting xlsx cell is an empty-string cell rather than a true null. This violates the task's declared contract ('value is set to null' on failure) and causes field_correct=false even when the extraction failure itself was legitimate.
diagnoses.wrong_approach: Formatting total via f'{total:.2f}' if total is not None else '' (or similar) and assigning the resulting string directly to the openpyxl cell / pandas DataFrame cell, so None is coerced to '' at the writeback boundary.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: Predictions row for 078.jpg: {'filename': '078.jpg', 'date': '2017-02-02', 'total_amount': ''} — total_amount is the empty string, not null. Verifier field_feedback: 078.jpg amount_correct=false. Task prompt explicitly declares: 'If extraction fails for either field, the value is set to null.' The empty-string cell cannot satisfy cell.value is None on readback.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: At the extraction/writeback boundary, preserve None end-to-end: return None (not '') from extract_total on failure, assign that None directly to the cell without string interpolation, and verify on reload that failed cells satisfy cell.value is None.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Separate 'formatting a present value' from 'writing an absent value': build a helper that returns f'{v:.2f}' when v is not None else None, pass that result unchanged to the cell, and add a post-save reload assertion (per xlsx 'Preserving null vs empty string on writeback') that any failed-extraction cell has cell.value is None.
diagnoses.scope_boundary: Scoped to tasks whose contract explicitly distinguishes null from empty string (as in this receipt task). Does not apply to tasks that accept '' as a sentinel, nor to formatted financial models where empty strings do not appear.
diagnoses.do_not_generalize_to: Do not force None-only semantics onto xlsx tasks whose contract uses '' or a placeholder string, and do not apply this to non-xlsx deliveries.
diagnoses.target_section: Structured Field Extraction from Receipts > Mechanism anchor: null_vs_empty_string_contract (with cross-reference to environment/skills/xlsx/SKILL.md > Preserving null vs empty string on writeback)

diagnoses.label: delivery_contract_self_check_not_executed_before_termination
diagnoses.general_pattern: The run terminates (max_iterations=65 hit; termination_reason=max_iterations) without reloading the written xlsx with data_only=True and asserting the declared schema: single 'results' sheet, three columns in order, rows sorted by filename, two-decimal strings for amounts, and null (not '') for failed extractions. A reload-and-assert step would have caught the 078.jpg empty-string cell before termination.
diagnoses.wrong_approach: Writing the workbook with openpyxl, running an in-memory sanity print, and terminating — without opening the saved file with load_workbook(path, data_only=True) and checking cell.value types/formats against the task contract.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: execution_metadata.termination_reason='max_iterations', acp_stop_reason='max_turn_requests', agent_iterations=65 with iteration_limit_hits=1; no verification exchange appears in the trajectory window reloading stat_ocr.xlsx with data_only=True and asserting cell.value is None for failed totals; delivered workbook contains total_amount='' for 078.jpg, which a reload-side assertion (cell.value is None) would have flagged.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: After wb.save(path), reload with openpyxl.load_workbook(path, data_only=True), assert sheet name, header order, row-sorted-by-filename, per-cell type/format, and specifically that failed-extraction cells have cell.value is None (not '').
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Add a mandatory pre-finish verification pass for data-only xlsx deliveries: load_workbook(path, data_only=True); check len(wb.sheetnames)==1 and the declared sheet name; check header equals the declared column list; iterate rows asserting (a) ordering, (b) regex ^\d+\.\d{2}$ or None for total_amount, (c) ISO date or None for date; only call finish once all assertions pass.
diagnoses.scope_boundary: Scoped to data-only xlsx outputs with a declared schema. Does not apply to financial models with formulas (which should use recalc.py and formula-error checks instead), nor to non-xlsx deliveries.
diagnoses.do_not_generalize_to: Do not run this reload-and-assert pass on formula-bearing workbooks (it would ignore formula correctness), and do not use it as a general assertion harness for unrelated tasks.
diagnoses.target_section: Delivery contract verification for data-only xlsx outputs

diagnoses.label: iteration_budget_exhausted_by_per_image_debug_loop
diagnoses.general_pattern: The agent runs a long interactive debug loop (think → OCR slice → tweak extract.py → rerun → compare) across many receipts, using 65/65 iterations and still terminating by budget rather than by convergence. The skill's own 'batch-diagnostic-then-batch-edit' workflow note is not followed: there is no single consolidated diagnostic dump + consolidated edit set + single re-run.
diagnoses.wrong_approach: Treating each failing receipt as an independent debugging episode (print per-variant OCR slice for a handful of files, hand-edit the extractor, rerun the whole batch, repeat), which consumes iterations without producing a reusable set of per-mechanism edits.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: execution_metadata.agent_iterations=65, max_iterations_at_source=65, termination_reason='max_iterations', iteration_limit_hits=1; response_tool_call_counts show terminal=27, think=22, file_editor=16 — a tight interactive loop; the exchange window shows repeated small str_replace edits to extract.py (e.g., e0024 → e0026 → e0027 dual-variant OCR, e0028 strict two-decimal regex) interleaved with per-image think notes rather than one consolidated diagnostic.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: Before per-image edits, dump a single table per receipt listing (variant, keyword line, tier, parsed value, corroboration anchors, current prediction). Diagnose patterns (e.g., 'same-tier intra-block outlier', 'one-decimal truncation', 'ambiguous DMY row'), plan a small set of mechanism-level edits that address several receipts at once, apply them in one commit, and re-run once.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Follow the 'Workflow note: batch-diagnostic-then-batch-edit' overlay: one diagnostic pass over all N images, one consolidated set of pattern/variant edits grouped by mechanism anchor (tier selection, two-decimal invariant, date locale, null-writeback), one re-run and one verification pass; avoid iteration-per-image loops that risk hitting max_iterations.
diagnoses.scope_boundary: Scoped to batch receipt-extraction tasks over many images where per-image debugging risks exhausting the iteration budget. Does not apply to single-document tasks or to tasks where per-item interactive debugging is cheap.
diagnoses.do_not_generalize_to: Do not import this batching discipline into tasks that genuinely require per-item interactive debugging (e.g., complex PDF form filling, financial-model repair) where mechanism-level batching would hide important per-item signal.
diagnoses.target_section: Structured Field Extraction from Receipts > Workflow note: batch-diagnostic-then-batch-edit

overlay.composition_issue: The current receipt overlay already defines tier priority, two-decimal invariant, null-writeback contract, locale binding, and the batch-diagnostic workflow note, but the trajectory shows the agent still (a) picks a corrupted same-tier outlier over a corroborated earlier candidate (074.jpg), (b) accepts one-decimal truncations padded to two decimals (064.jpg), (c) writes '' instead of None on extraction failure (078.jpg), and (d) exhausts the iteration budget in a per-image loop rather than a consolidated diagnostic pass. These are not missing mechanisms but under-specified decision procedures inside existing anchors: intra-tier corroboration is not operationalized, the two-decimal invariant is enforced at formatting only, the null-vs-empty contract is not enforced at the openpyxl assignment boundary, and the batch-diagnostic note is not tied to a hard pre-finish verification step. Strengthen (not add) multi_variant_consensus_over_tier_priority with explicit intra-tier corroboration scoring and tighten the cross-references between monetary_two_decimal_invariant, null_vs_empty_string_contract, and the xlsx delivery_contract_self_check.
preservation_constraints: Preserve the strict tier priority ordering (GRAND TOTAL > TOTAL RM / TOTAL: RM > TOTAL AMOUNT > TOTAL / AMOUNT / TOTAL DUE / AMOUNT DUE / BALANCE DUE / NETT TOTAL / NET TOTAL) exactly as declared by the task prompt; corroboration scoring must never override a cleanly-anchored higher-priority tier.

Preserve the receipt-only scope of the overlay and the explicit negative boundaries that forbid importing receipt-specific heuristics into openai-vision, pdf, video-frame-extraction, or into generic xlsx guidance.
Preserve the existing summary-section cutoff rule (GST/Tax/SST SUMMARY, tabular column headers) and the exclusion-keyword list; do not relax these when adding intra-tier corroboration.

Preserve the receipt-scoped null-vs-empty-string contract and its cross-reference to xlsx 'Preserving null vs empty string on writeback'; do not promote None-only semantics to tasks whose contract uses '' or a placeholder.
Preserve the 'conditional_multi_pass_ocr_on_noisy_numeric_fields' guidance (multi-variant OCR as a conditional fallback, not an unconditional sweep) when strengthening cross-variant selection.
Preserve the batch-diagnostic-then-batch-edit workflow note's scope (batch OCR over many images) and do not force it onto single-document or interactive-debug tasks.

package_assessment.rationale: All diagnosed failures are controllable by the image-ocr receipt overlay and the xlsx data-only writeback section already present in the current candidate skills. (1) 074.jpg wrong amount is an intra-tier candidate-selection defect addressable by strengthening multi_variant_consensus_over_tier_priority with corroboration scoring against Subtotal/Payment/Change. (2) 064.jpg wrong amount is addressable by enforcing the existing monetary_two_decimal_invariant at candidate selection (not just formatting) and preferring cross-variant two-decimal matches on the same tier. (3) 034.jpg wrong date is addressable by executing the batch-dominance clause already present in receipt_date_label_binding_and_locale. (4) 078.jpg wrong amount ('' vs null) is directly addressable by null_vs_empty_string_contract and its xlsx cross-reference. (5) Termination by max_iterations is addressable by the existing batch-diagnostic-then-batch-edit workflow note plus the xlsx delivery_contract_self_check as a pre-finish gate. No infrastructure or executor-only failure is required to explain the observed field errors; the verifier reports delivery_status=valid with model_calls=0, confirming the failures sit inside skill-controllable logic rather than in the executor, verifier, or image/channel provenance.
